rubrics.justification: Description is broadly consistent with the provided 2AA label, but it relies heavily on the lab grade and includes features not confidently verifiable from a single static image, such as absence of debris/fragmentation and detailed TE assessment.

Integrates age, PCOS, prior biochemical pregnancy, endometrial thickness, ovarian response, sperm parameters, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis; only minor overstatements such as equating biochemical pregnancy with confirmed uterine receptivity.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with conclusions generally supported by embryo quality and patient factors; minor issues include somewhat optimistic interpretation of prior biochemical pregnancy and implantation estimate.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice guidelines, especially support for single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst; slight deviations include calling 2AA unequivocally top-tier and suggesting PGT-A somewhat broadly.
Provides practical next steps including SET, luteal support, cryopreservation, monitoring, and future-cycle considerations; useful but somewhat generic and lacking finer protocol-specific nuance.
